messages:
Alice Zhang: Heads up — nightly perf dash just alerted: +12% p99 latency on short-sequence workloads since the 4821 merge. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/reports/rl-1977 :eyes:
Ben Rogers: I saw that. 4821 changed the kernel selection thresholds (0.7 -> 0.9) and tuned score decay. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4821 commit abcdef1
Carol Nguyen: Can confirm in local canary (small fleet) — short sequences are falling back to generic_v2 kernel more often, which has worse startup cost for these cases.
Dmitri Ivanov: Ran a quick profile on a repro trace: execpath time jumped, kernel selector log shows: "selected kernel=generic_v2 score=0.92 threshold=0.9" for sequences length 8-12. Full snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T03:12:04Z] kernel_selector: features={seq_len:9, ffw:0.6} scores={optimized_v1:0.88, generic_v2:0.92} selected=generic_v2
```
Carol Nguyen: that matches. If we lower threshold back to 0.7 locally, p99 drops ~11% in the repro harness.
nightly-bot: CI perf check failed — job: nightly-ci/perf-compare (link: https://ci.internal/runs/13721) ; baseline vs head shows regressions in p95/p99 for small seq workloads.
Eve Martinez: Is 4821 on the canary rollout? We might need to pause to avoid user impact.
Ben Rogers: It was a staged rollout (10% -> 30%). Canary still at 30%. I've paused further rollout in console and pinned the model to previous variant for the 30% cohort.
Alice Zhang: Can we bisect to confirm 4821 is the root cause instead of unrelated infra noise? Steps?
Dmitri Ivanov: Quick bisect approach I used: 1) checkout main@pre-4821 2) build selector image 3) deploy to a small canary pool 4) run the short-seq perf harness. I have the script: `scripts/perf/bisect_selector.sh --from=main~5 --to=main` — it flagged commit abcdef1.
Carol Nguyen: I pushed a hotfix branch that reverts the threshold change and keeps the other selector improvements (w/ fallback guard). PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4838 — small test matrix green locally.
Ben Rogers: Nice. Can we do a staged revert (canary -> 100%) or prefer an explicit revert PR? Given this touches kernel selection, safer to revert the threshold-only change via PR so CI runs full regression checks.
Alice Zhang: Agreed. Ben, can you open the revert PR if Carol can't? We need a short rollback timeline.
Ben Rogers: Opened PR 4839 (revert: abcdef1). CI: https://ci.internal/runs/13728 — added perf compare job and a canary deploy job.
nightly-bot: Canary deploy triggered for revert PR 4839 (canary pool: t2-small, cohort=5%)
Eve Martinez: Deployed revert to 5% canary. Monitoring p99 — currently within noise at +0.5% vs baseline after revert. :thumbsup:
Dmitri Ivanov: Re-ran profiler on the canary with revert — selector logs show selection of optimized_v1 for same traces: `selected kernel=optimized_v1 score=0.88 threshold=0.7` and execpath restored.
Carol Nguyen: Running larger greenhouse run overnight to be safe. If green, promote revert quickly.
Alice Zhang: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: 1) Add a unit/regression test that covers short-sequence kernel preference (Carol) 2) Add a perf check in PR template for kernel selection changes (Ben) 3) Investigate whether model-specific heuristics would avoid a global threshold tweak (Dmitri).
Eve Martinez: I'll update the rollout playbook with steps we used here and add a quick checklist for kernel selector changes.
Ben Rogers: Merge revert PR 4839 approved and merged at 1977654800. Monitoring shows p99 back to baseline across canaries and prod cohorts held.
Alice Zhang: Closing triage — mark incident as mitigated, but keep monitoring for 24h. Thanks :sparkles:
